en.text:
A task list forgets the moment you tick the box. My AI agent forgot the moment the session ended.

I got tired of solving things twice and explaining my project every morning, so I built Tisty: a memory on my own disk, for me and for my agent.

How do you keep yours?

This is how Tisty does it:

https://www.tisty.app

Every morning I explained my project to my AI agent again. Same stack, same decisions, same dead ends.

I built Tisty so it starts from what moved since yesterday and the task it was on, not from a blank chat.

How do you start a session without the recap?

Eight months after I fixed some timeouts on save, they came back somewhere else. I remembered solving it. I couldn't remember how: the note went when I ticked the task.

So in Tisty a finished task is kept whole, steps and notes.

Where do your solved problems end up?

I don't want to find out what my agent deletes by mistake.

So Tisty gives it no delete at all: it marks what looks old and says why, and I decide. If I wrote while it was thinking, it has to read again before writing.

Too strict? What would you change?

An agent that needs one paragraph will read the whole document to find it.

In Tisty it reads the outline first, with what each section weighs, then only that section: about 3% of a 256 KB file, 12% at worst.

How do you keep yours from reading everything?

A document cites another. A task was born from an idea. In my notes all of that is true and none of it shows: each link lives inside its own file.

I'm designing a map of it for Tisty, tasks and documents together.

What would you want to see first on yours?

An agent's automatic memory keeps what it guessed mattered, and yesterday's decision next to today's.

In Tisty what my agent remembers is documents I can read and correct, and a changed decision is struck through with its date.

Do you ever read what your agent remembers?

The best answer an AI gave me last month is in a chat I can't find any more.

Now, when a chat gets something right, I ask the agent to write it into a document in Tisty, on my disk, where search finds it.

Where do you keep what a chat got right?

I can't control what my AI tools send home. I can control where my notes live.

So in Tisty they stay on my disk, as Markdown: there is no server of mine to send them to. What an agent reads from them still travels with that agent.

Where do you draw that line?

A memory only helps if the agent opens it. Tisty asks every agent to start from what moved, and some still skip it unless I remind them.

Next for Tisty's plugin: ask it when the session starts, with no reminder.

How do you make your agent check its notes first?

My NOTES.md went stale in a week. Then came one notes file per session, and they piled up until neither my agent nor I trusted them.

What I do now in Tisty: one page per subject, corrected in place.

Has anyone kept an agent's notes honest for months? How?

I can read every note my agent keeps. What I can't see is how they connect: what leads where, what nothing points to.

So I'm designing a map for Tisty: each document and task a neuron, each link a connection.

What would you check first on yours?

Long session, and my agent no longer remembers what we agreed at the start. The usual advice: open a new chat.

So the state can't live in the chat. In Tisty the agent ticks each step and notes what's left, and a fresh chat picks up there.

How do you survive compaction?

Every MCP server I connect spends context before the agent does anything. Mine too.

So I cut Tisty's tool descriptions by a third, and a test fails if they grow back.

Is that enough? What should Tisty trim next?

My agent can read all my code. It can't read why I rejected option B three months ago, so it proposes B again.

In Tisty I keep each decision with its date and its why, in the document on that subject.

Where do you write down the why, so it gets read?

I can see where a note points. I can't see what points at it, so I never know what a change will break.

Working on it for Tisty: beside each document, who cites it and in which section.

Do you use backlinks, or do you just search?

The bank paperwork comes back every year, and every year I work it out again from zero.

Now I do it as a task in Tisty, with its steps and notes, and next year the archive tells me how it went.

How do you remember the things you only do once a year?

"Done", says the agent. Sometimes it is.

In Tisty an agent can only say a task is done: it waits there until I confirm it or send it back.

How do you handle it? How could we make this better in Tisty?

An agent searching my notes opens every file that matches, just to find one sentence.

In Tisty a search answers with the line that says it, ten results at a time. It opens a file only if the line isn't enough.

How does yours search without reading it all?

A search by similarity finds notes that look alike. It can't tell me they're related, or which one is still true.

The map I'm designing for Tisty starts from what is written: a citation, a mention, a tag. Every link can explain itself.

Would you want guessed links too?

My work log grew to 256 KB and my agent reread all of it every session.

With Tisty it asks what moved and reads only that: about 1% when nothing changed. Under ~50 KB a plain file is still cheaper.

How do you keep long notes from eating the context?

I used to close the laptop mid-task and start the next day from a blank chat.

Now, before closing, I tell the agent: note what we did, what failed and what's left. In Tisty that is one request, leave off.

What's your end-of-session habit?

Each of my agents keeps its own memory. What I told Claude Code, Codex never heard.

So I moved it outside them all: Tisty, over MCP, where every note says which agent wrote it.

How do you share context between agents?

Reviewing what an agent wrote takes me longer than it took to write.

So I review earlier: in Tisty it first writes the plan as a task with steps, and I read that before it touches anything.

Where do you put the checkpoint: before, during or after?

I ask my agent for one thing and it comes back with three, two of them nobody wanted.

What helps me: in Tisty a task says "Done when" before the work starts, and its document says what is out of scope.

How do you tell an agent where to stop?

To learn who cites a document, my agent has to open them all. Tisty has no index of links yet.

I'm designing one, made on my machine from what I already wrote: no extra files, nothing written for the machine.

What should an agent know about a note before opening it?

An agent changed a note I had open, and I found out days later.

In Tisty when something writes in the document in front of me, the window says so and offers to go back to what it said before.

How do you notice what an agent changed in your files?

Every new session opens the same long document again, just to see whether it needs it.

In Tisty an agent that read a long document leaves a summary for the next one, and it is marked stale when the document changes.

How do your agents share what they already read?

Agents add to their notes and never prune. Months later the same subject lives in four places.

Today in Tisty the outline points at what repeats, and my agent merges it when I ask. I'm working on one request that does the whole pass.

Who prunes your agent's memory?

A summary is only safe if I can see what it threw away.

In Tisty when my agent folds its notes on a task into one digest, the lines I wrote stay, and I can ask for the notes back as they were.

How do you check what compaction dropped?

Not everything I write down is for an AI to read.

So the Diary in Tisty stays closed to agents until I open it, and even then they only add to the end of today.

What do you keep away from your assistant, and how?
